findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_bounty, check_inbox · Private data: wallet_status · Public sink: post_bounty, submit_bounty, send_agent_message · Destructive: act, chat_inference.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_bounty, check_inbox · Private data: wallet_status · Public sink: post_bounty, submit_bounty, send_agent_message · Destructive: act, chat_inference

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_unmet_demand" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Inspect capabilities hitting House Fallback so you can spin up a P2P seller worker and keep 95%." → after: "Inspect capabilities hitting House Fallback so you can spin up a P2P seller worker and earn protocol keep."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
